In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for PDES, the number of cores is more important than the size of caches, and that the best architecture design is one that is heterogeneous with a mix of out-of-order and in-order cores.
for PDES on multicore systems, a heterogeneous architecture with 8 in-order cores and 8 out-of-order cores is a good design point in terms performance, scalability, area and power consumption.
PDES is scalable and performs well on multicore and many-core platforms, but the performance is sensitive to the underlying architecture design choices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best performance for PDES on a given chip area is achieved with a homogeneous design that uses out-of-order cores and large caches, and the best scalability is obtained with a heterogeneous system with both in-order and out-order cores.

PDES performance and scaling is highly sensitive to the design choices made in a many-core architecture and that object partitioning can significantly reduce communication overhead in heterogeneous many-core systems.
PDES can scale to manycores, but the scalability is dependent on the architecture design choices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best design point for PDES is a small number of out-of-order cores, and that object partitioning is not very helpful in heterogeneous systems.
